notes:
Summary: RapidQuill is building a low-latency VS Code copilot extension (IDEKit) focused on streaming inline completions and token-efficient assistants. Team: CTO (Eve Santos), Head of Product (Liam Park), Eng leads for editor integration. POC: 2-week editor plugin POC running against Redwood hosted API + local dev proxy.

Key asks / requirements: streaming responses with sub-100ms first-token for inline suggestion UX; per-developer rate limits and burst protection; model pinning per-customer and per-route fallback rules; token-cost visibility (per-route), prefix/KV cache hints to reduce cost; offline-mode for local tokenized completions during dev tests.

Security/compliance: needs SSO/SAML + SCIM, audit logs pushed to SIEM, KMS for customer keys, option for VPC peering for dedicated. Data residency: EU customers need region pinning.

Quotes: "We need inline suggestions to feel instant — anything over 120ms is noticeable." — Eng lead.

Sales notes: demo of streaming completion on 2024-10-12 (recording + ff id). POC_started 2024-11-01; delivered baseline latency report 2024-11-15. Cost sensitivity: high for small teams, flexible for enterprise if SLA and private deployment offered.

Next immediate: align on POC success metrics (latency SLA, token cost baseline, telemetry hooks), security questionnaire answers to be returned by 2024-11-25. Blockers: security ops still needs encryption-at-rest confirmation; legal wants SLAs for model-fallback behavior.
